title.narrative: Sustainable Islands: Building Heritage Disaster and Climate Resilience of Small Islands Developing States in the Pacific region

description.narrative: The Pacific is one of the world’s most disaster-prone regions. While many SIDS have developed national disaster management plans, the protection of culture and heritage has scarcely been taken into consideration, due to the lack of awareness of the impact of climate change on heritage, insufficient understanding of heritage as an enabler for sustainable development, as well as the lack of specialized capacities and dedicated resources. This project aims to support targeted SIDS countries in the Pacific region to build heritage resilience through capacity-building and community-based activities on disaster and risk management, with particular focus on risks related to climate change and natural disasters on heritage sites. The project will involve four(4) to five (5) countries in the Pacific region who will benefit from capacity-building on heritage disaster and risk management, which will be conducted as part of a regional workshop, as well as through the organization of sub-regional capacity-building sessions (online or on-site) on disaster risk management planning and climate adaptation at heritage sites, followed by three (3) concrete implementation cases to support the development and implementation of the Disaster and Risk Management Plan/Climate Change Adaptation Plan at specific heritage sites.
